source_changes.old: 1.1 Choose a finite bundle atlas and a subordinate finite smooth partition of unity using compactness and [F1, F2]. In each chart multiply a section coefficient by its partition function, extend by zero within the chart, convolve with a fixed compactly supported smooth mollifier of radius $\delta$, and sum the finitely many resulting local sections. For each $\delta>0$ this defines a linear operator $S_\delta:C^0(M,E)\to\Gamma^\infty(E)$: every output derivative is an integral of the input against a derivative of a fixed smooth kernel, so each $C^r$ seminorm is bounded by a finite constant times the input $C^0$ norm. Uniform continuity of each input on compact chart supports gives $\|S_\delta u-u\|_{C^0}\to0$ for every $u$. Since $x\mapsto s(x,\cdot)$ has compact image in $C^0(M,E)$, a finite subcover argument makes this convergence uniform over $x\in X$. [given, F1, F2, given, construct]
source_changes.new: 1.1 If $X$ is empty, take the unique empty family. If $M$ is empty, its bundle has the unique empty smooth section, and take the unique family of those sections. In either case all agreement constraints and the straight-line homotopy hold vacuously, and the displayed error is $\sup\{0\}=0$. We may therefore assume $X$ and $M$ nonempty. empty_boundary_after.evidence: Statement and step 1.1: the error is the real supremum of {0} union the set of nonnegative pointwise errors. If X or M is empty this set is {0}, so the unique empty family or family of empty sections has error zero and satisfies the relative homotopy conditions. On nonempty products adding zero does not change the error. Empty K and q=0 still omit the collar and marked-point corrections in steps 2.1 and 3.1.
